in_short: This is the most sensitive page on the site. Owners arrive on it from an email link whose address ends in a session token.

It gets the same Google tag as every other page, and the tag is built so that the token can never be sent: the address is cut off at the # before Analytics sees it. A test with a fake token confirms it.
It now also tells you how often a reset works, fails, or arrives too late.
6 changes are on the branch: 3 technical, 3 tracking. Nothing changed for ranking or in the text.

needs_you_intro: One choice is yours. I took the option that tells you more and still sends nothing sensitive.

needs_you.title: If you would rather have no analytics on this page at all
needs_you.detail: The safest possible version of this page has no third-party script on it. I added the tag because the three events are useful and the token cannot reach it. If you prefer zero risk over the numbers, say so and I take the tag off this one page. The cookie notice and click names would stay.
needs_you.action: Tell me "no analytics on the reset page" if that is what you want.

changes_intro: Everything below is committed on `claude/practical-keller-adcqrc`. The page looks the same.

changes.title: Google Analytics added, with the address cut at #
changes.why: The email link opens `reset-password.html#access_token=…`. The tag passes Analytics the address up to the # and nothing after it. The check for this page opens it with a fake token and confirms the token appears nowhere in what the tag would send.

changes.title: Three events: done, failed, link expired
changes.why: `password_reset_done` fires when the new password is saved. `password_reset_failed` fires when Supabase refuses it. `password_reset_link_invalid` fires when the page opens without a valid link, which is what an owner sees after waiting too long. If that last one is common, the link lifetime in Supabase is too short. None of them carries the password.

changes.title: `cta_click` on 6 links, and the cookie notice
changes.why: `reset_done_login` shows how many owners go straight on to log in. The cookie notice comes with `site.js`.
changes.after: nav_home · reset_done_login · reset_request_new · reset_login · footer_email · footer_instagram

changes.title: Icons and language, as on the homepage
changes.why: Added the `favicon.ico` fallback, the iPhone icon and `theme-color`, and set `lang="en-US"`.

changes.title: Same font request as the homepage
changes.why: The page now sends the identical request, so a visitor arriving from the homepage already has it cached.

changes.title: Taller tap areas
changes.why: "Back to Rihla" in the top bar was 18 px tall and the footer links 17 px. They are now 42 px and 29 px to tap. Nothing moved.

verify_intro: Do these once the branch is published.
verify: Ask for a reset link for an account you own and follow it. Setting a new password should work as before.
In GA4, open Reports, then Realtime, after accepting cookies. `password_reset_done` should appear, and the page address shown should end at `reset-password.html`, with nothing after it.

files.change: Google tag, three events, click names, icons, fonts, tap areas

method: Audited from the repository and rendered in headless Chrome on a local copy of the site. 26 common checks and 8 page checks pass: valid link, refused password, accepted password, no link, library blocked, and the token test.
The checks run against a stand-in for Supabase's library. No password in your Supabase project was changed.
The layout-shift figures were taken without a valid link, so they include the "link expired" message appearing. They are a guide only.
The live site and the public CDN are unreachable from the audit sandbox, so nothing here was checked in production.
